full_text_en:
Sun Changrong v. Jilin Provincial People's Government — dispute over decision not to accept administrative reconsideration

【Ruling Summary】

"Government information" as regulated by the Regulations on Open Government Information refers to information that actually exists and is recorded or preserved in a certain form. A request to learn about the validity of a document is of a consulting nature and does not fall within the category of government information that "shall be provided in the form requested by the applicant" as stipulated in Article 26 of the said Regulations. The response or failure to respond by an administrative organ to a consulting request does not constitute an act of government information disclosure, nor does it have any substantive impact on the rights and obligations of the consultant. Therefore, it is not within the scope of acceptance for administrative reconsideration. A plaintiff who lacks a legally protected interest lacks standing, and the people's court may either refuse to accept the case or rule to dismiss the lawsuit.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Xing Ti Zi No. 19

Re-review Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Sun Changrong, male, born March 13, 1950, Han ethnicity, residing in Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Re-review Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Jilin Provincial People's Government, domiciled at No. 329 Xinfa Road, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Chaoliang, Governor of the Province.

Agent ad litem: Yan Min, staff member of the Legal Affairs Office of the Jilin Provincial People's Government.

Agent ad litem: Yan Chunmei, staff member of the Legal Affairs Office of the Jilin Provincial People's Government.

In the case of Sun Changrong, the re-review applicant, v. the Jilin Provincial People's Government regarding a decision not to accept administrative reconsideration, the Jilin High People's Court rendered an administrative judgment on December 29, 2011, [(2011) Ji Xing Zhong Zi No. 21], which has become legally effective. Dissatisfied, Sun Changrong applied to this Court for re-review. On September 26, 2014, this Court issued an administrative ruling [(2012) Xing Jian Zi No. 682] to bring the case before this Court for a retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel consisting of Presiding Judge Ma Yongxin, Judge Liang Fengyun, and Acting Judge Hu Wenli to hear this case. The trial of this case has now concluded.

The First Instance trial by the Changchun Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province found: In 2010, Sun Changrong applied to the Changchun Real Estate Administration Bureau of Jilin Province to change the use of his house from "residential" to "commercial." The registration authority stated that, in accordance with the Notice on Issues Concerning Applications for Change of House Use Registration (Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27, hereinafter "Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27") issued by the Jilin Provincial Department of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (hereinafter "Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D.") on November 17, 1999, a change of use required planning permission. After the planning department refused to grant the corresponding administrative license, in February 2011, Sun Changrong submitted an application to the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. requesting to ascertain whether the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 was still effective and also requesting a written reply. The Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. did not provide a written reply. On April 26, 2011, Sun Changrong filed an administrative reconsideration application with the Jilin Provincial People's Government, on the grounds that the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. had prevaricated and failed to give a written reply to his application, requesting that, in accordance with the Regulations on Open Government Information of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Regulations on Open Government Information") and relevant legal provisions, the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. be ordered to give a written reply according to law. On April 28, 2011, the Jilin Provincial People's Government issued a Decision Not to Accept Administrative Reconsideration [Ji Zheng Fu Bu Zi [2011] No. __], holding that Sun Changrong's application for administrative reconsideration did not fall within the scope of administrative reconsideration, and, in accordance with Articles 6 and 17 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Administrative Reconsideration Law"), decided not to accept the application. On May 31, 2011, the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. published on its website the abolition of the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice. On July 6, 2011, Sun Changrong filed an administrative lawsuit with the Changchun Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province, requesting the court to revoke the Decision Not to Accept Administrative Reconsideration [Ji Zheng Fu Bu Zi [2011] No. __] issued by the Jilin Provincial People's Government and to order it to re-make an administrative act.

The court of first instance held: Plaintiff Sun Changrong applied for reconsideration to the defendant, the Jilin Provincial People's Government, on the grounds that the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. had not fulfilled its duty to provide information on whether the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 was still valid and to give a written reply, requesting the defendant to order the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. to give a clear written reply according to law. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, the matter for which plaintiff Sun Changrong applied for administrative reconsideration did not fall within the scope of administrative reconsideration. Therefore, the defendant, the Jilin Provincial People's Government, correctly decided not to accept the application on the grounds that Sun Changrong's administrative reconsideration application concerning the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D.'s failure to fulfill its duty of government information disclosure was not within the scope of administrative reconsideration, in accordance with Articles 6 and 17 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law. Plaintiff Sun Changrong's argument that the defendant's decision not to accept violated relevant legal provisions and his request that the court revoke the Decision Not to Accept [Ji Zheng Fu Bu Zi [2011] No. __] according to law were unfounded, and the court did not support his claims. In summary, the defendant's decision not to accept the plaintiff's application was based on clear facts, correctly applied laws and regulations, and was in compliance with legal procedures. Pursuant to Article 54(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Administrative Procedure Law"), the court rendered an administrative judgment [(2011) Chang Xing Chu Zi No. 1], upholding the Decision Not to Accept Administrative Reconsideration issued by the Jilin Provincial People's Government on April 28, 2011.

Dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, Sun Changrong appealed to the Jilin High People's Court. The court of second instance confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held: Sun Changrong, due to his personal interest, applied to the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. for a written confirmation of whether the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice was still valid. The conduct of the staff of the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D., who gave an oral reply (without providing a written reply), was not explicitly provided by law as a matter for which an application for administrative reconsideration could be made. The Jilin Provincial People's Government's decision not to accept the reconsideration application, on the grounds that the conduct of the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. did not constitute a "specific administrative act" within the meaning of Article 33(2) of the Regulations on Open Government Information for which administrative reconsideration could be applied, was not clearly illegal or improper. The first instance judgment was based on clear facts, correctly applied the law, and followed legal procedures, and should be upheld. Pursuant to Article 61(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law, the court rendered an administrative judgment [(2011) Ji Xing Zhong Zi No. 21], dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, Sun Changrong applied to this Court for a retrial, arguing: The Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D.'s application for verification of the validity of the document was only answered orally, not in writing as requested, which constituted a failure to fulfill its duty of government information disclosure according to law; the administrative reconsideration application against the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D.'s failure to fulfill its duty of government information disclosure should have been accepted by the Jilin Provincial People's Government. The first instance court held that the matter of reconsideration did not fall within the scope of acceptance under Article 6 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law, and the second instance court held that the oral reply (without a written reply) by the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. did not constitute a "specific administrative act" under Article 33(2) of the Regulations on Open Government Information. Both courts found that the Jilin Provincial People's Government's decision not to accept administrative reconsideration was not illegal, but these views constituted an error in the application of law. He requested the Supreme People's Court to revoke the original judgments, revoke the contested decision not to accept, and order the respondent to re-make an administrative act according to law.

The Jilin Provincial People's Government submitted its opinion: Sun Changrong's request to the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. to verify whether the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice was valid was a consulting act and had nothing to do with government information disclosure. Since the law does not impose an obligation to provide a written reply, the decision not to accept the reconsideration application as the reconsideration authority was proper. Moreover, if an administrative organ fails to perform its duty in response to an application for government information disclosure, citizens, legal persons, or other organizations may only seek relief through the reporting channel under Article 33(1) of the Regulations on Open Government Information. Furthermore, the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice had a basis in higher-level laws such as the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. Sun Changrong had lost a lawsuit against the Changchun Planning Bureau of Jilin Province regarding the failure to change the original planning permission, so whether the document Sun Changrong sought to verify was valid did not affect his substantive rights. Sun Changrong's application for retrial was aimed at pressuring the court to compel the housing and planning departments to change the use of his house.

This Court, upon trial, confirms the facts found in the original trials. It is also found that the content of the application submitted by Sun Changrong to the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. in this case is: "The Notice on Issues Concerning Applications for Change of House Use Registration (Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27) issued by your department on November 17, 1999, has, according to the relevant provisions of the Jilin Provincial Regulations and Normative Documents Cleanup Measures (Jilin Provincial People's Government Decree No. 201), been out of time. I would like to know if it is still effective? Please give a written reply." At the time Sun Changrong applied to the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. to learn whether the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice was valid, the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. was, in accordance with the requirements of the Notice on Relevant Issues Concerning the Cleanup of Regulations and Normative Documents (Ji Fu Fa [2010] No. 74), organizing and carrying out the cleanup of normative documents, including the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice. In response to Sun Changrong's application, the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. gave an oral reply. The above facts are confirmed by the application submitted by Sun Changrong to the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. on February 20, 2011, the announcement of the results of the normative document cleanup directory published by the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. on May 31, 2011, and the first instance trial transcript.

This Court holds: Article 2 of the Regulations on Open Government Information provides: "For the purposes of these Regulations, 'government information' means information that is produced or obtained by an administrative organ in the course of performing its duties and that is recorded or preserved in a certain form." Accordingly, the government information referred to in these Regulations should be existing information that is recorded or preserved in a certain form. To accurately grasp the scope of application of government information, Article 2 of the Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Doing a Good Job of Handling Applications for Government Information Disclosure (Guo Ban Fa [2010] No. 5) clearly stipulates: "The government information provided by an administrative organ to an applicant should be existing information; generally, it does not require the administrative organ to summarize, process, or re-create (except for processing distinctions)." In this case, what Sun Changrong applied to learn from the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. was the validity of the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice. This was not an application for the disclosure of the government document itself "recorded or preserved in a certain form." In nature, it was a consultation and does not fall within the scope regulated by the Regulations on Open Government Information. Moreover, making a reply or not making a reply to a consultation will not have any substantive impact on the consultant's rights and obligations. Therefore, the Jilin Provincial People's Government's decision not to accept the administrative reconsideration application is consistent with Articles 6 and 17 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law. Sun Changrong's argument that the Jilin Provincial People's Government violated the Regulations on Open Government Information and relevant legal provisions, and his request that the people's court revoke the decision not to accept according to law, are unfounded and this Court does not support them. The first and second instance courts did not err in upholding the Jilin Provincial People's Government's decision not to accept.

According to Article 26 of the Regulations on Open Government Information, government information provided by an administrative organ upon application should be provided in the form requested by the applicant. In this case, since Sun Changrong's application was of a consulting nature, it does not fall within the category of "shall be provided in the form requested by the applicant" as provided in that article. For such consulting applications, the law does not explicitly require that the administrative organ must provide a written reply. Given that the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. had already given an oral reply, and especially given that before Sun Changrong filed this lawsuit, the Jilin Provincial D.H.U.R.D. had already announced the abolition of the Ji Jian Fang Zi [1999] No. 27 notice, Sun Changrong's request that the people's court order the administrative organ to reply on the validity of that notice has no actual interest that deserves judicial protection. The basis for his request that the respondent re-make an administrative act has been lost.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 89(1)(1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 76 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The administrative judgment of the Jilin High People's Court [(2011) Ji Xing Zhong Zi No. 21] is affirmed.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Ma Yongxin

Judge: Liang Fengyun

Acting Judge: Hu Wenli

May 12, 2016

Clerk: Li Lintao

[Brief Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Ma Yongxin, Senior Judge, born in 1966, Master of Laws, appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2006.
